paper_summary: Japanese-language JSME conference paper (2003) on the toughening mechanism of glass-microballoon (GM) filled epoxy by liquid CTBN rubber modification. Four materials were cast and cured at 120 C for 16 h from Epikote 828 epoxy + B-002 hardener: neat 828, rubber-modified 828R (CTBN 1300x9), GM-filled 828G (3M A16 surface-treated glass microballoons) and rubber-modified GM-filled 828RG. Three-point bending and SENB fracture-toughness tests (quasi-static 1 mm/min and impact 1 m/s) show that rubber modification lowers flexural strength slightly but roughly doubles the static GIC and triples the impact GIC of the GM-filled foam, and nearly doubles its fracture absorbed energy; SEM attributes the improvement to shear plastic deformation around rubber particles plus GM/epoxy interfacial debonding.

extraction_notes: Source is a 2-page Japanese JSME annual-meeting extended abstract with heavy OCR corruption; text was read in full. (1) The only tabulated numbers are Table 1: flexural strength sigma = 125, 109, 36.4, 30.6 MPa and fracture absorbed energy U = 38.8, 47.1, 1.99, 3.78 kJ/m^2 for 828, 828R, 828G, 828RG respectively (the table label '838RG' is an OCR error for 828RG). The mapping of the concatenated OCR digit strings to columns is confirmed by the text, which states that rubber modification slightly lowers flexural strength while raising absorbed energy, with the largest relative increase for the GM-filled material. (2) U is reported in kJ/m^2 (energy divided by specimen cross-sectional area, eq. 3), which is dimensionally different from the schema field energy_absorption_mj_m3 (MJ/m^3), so it was NOT written into that field to avoid a unit error; it is preserved here: 828 = 38.8, 828R = 47.1, 828G = 1.99, 828RG = 3.78 kJ/m^2. (3) Fracture toughness GIC (static, 1 mm/min, and impact, 1 m/s) appears only in Fig. 2 as a bar chart with no tabulated values; the text only states that rubber modification raises static GIC of the GM-filled material by about 2x and impact GIC by about 3x, so all GIC values were left out. The schema also has no fracture-toughness field. (4) Relative density appears only in Fig. 1 normalised to 828 = 1 (828G falls to about half); no absolute density in g/cm^3 is given, so measured_density_g_cc is null everywhere. (5) particle_weight_fraction for the filled foams was computed from the parts-by-weight formulations given in Sec. 2.1 (numbers in parentheses are parts per 100 parts of base resin): 828G = 10/(100+10+50) = 0.063; 828RG = 10/(100+10+10+50) = 0.059. These are derived, not stated verbatim. Particle volume fraction is not reported. (6) Neither test temperature nor strain rate is stated for the bending tests, so both are null; loading rate was 10 mm/min. (7) The unfilled 828 and 828R baselines are included as records with particle_weight_fraction = 0.0 (particle_type still set to glass_microballoon since the schema has no 'none' option) to preserve the composition series.
